sentences.nl: Martin, Marieke en Gianluca zijn bij de huisarts.
sentences.en: Martin, Marieke, and Gianluca are at the general practitioner's.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Martin, Marieke and Gianluca are at the general practitioner.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present tense "zijn" (are) for the verb "to be."  
• The preposition "bij" is used to indicate location, equivalent to "at" in English.  
• "Huisarts" is a compound noun: "huis" (house) + "arts" (doctor), meaning "general practitioner" or "family doctor."

Extra examples:  
• Ik ben bij de bakker. (I am at the baker's.)  
• Zij zijn bij hun oma. (They are at their grandma's.)  
• We zijn bij de tandarts. (We are at the dentist's.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa en Tom zijn bij de kapper. (Lisa and Tom are at the hairdresser's.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Visiting the huisarts is common for non-emergency health concerns in the Netherlands. The huisarts often serves as the first point of contact before seeing a specialist.

sentences.nl: Gianluca is gevallen.
sentences.en: Gianluca has fallen.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Gianluca is fallen.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Is gevallen" is the perfect tense in Dutch, formed with the auxiliary verb "is" (to be) and the past participle "gevallen" (fallen). This construction is used to describe actions that have been completed.  
• Word order: In Dutch, the auxiliary verb comes second, and the past participle typically comes at the end of the clause.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij is naar huis gegaan." (He has gone home.)  
  - "Zij is dokter geworden." (She has become a doctor.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Lotte is naar de stad gefietst." (Lotte has cycled to the city.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch, the verb "vallen" (to fall) can be used both literally and figuratively, similar to English. For instance, "vallen" can describe someone falling down or "in slaap vallen" (to fall asleep).

sentences.nl: Hij heeft pijn.
sentences.en: He is in pain.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He has pain.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present tense verb "heeft" (has) to indicate possession. The word "pijn" (pain) is a noun. In Dutch, expressing that someone is in pain often uses the structure "hij/zij heeft" followed by the noun for what is being felt.  
• Example 1: "Zij heeft honger." (She is hungry.)  
• Example 2: "Wij hebben dorst." (We are thirsty.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij heeft koorts." (She has a fever.)

sentences.nl: Marieke is met Gianluca, in de spreekkamer van de dokter.
sentences.en: Marieke is with Gianluca in the doctor's consulting room.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke is with Gianluca, in the consultation room of the doctor.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "is met" to indicate accompaniment or presence. "Met" is a preposition meaning "with."  
• "In de spreekkamer" refers to a specific location, using "in" (in) and "de" (the) to specify "the consultation room."  
• "Van de dokter" uses "van" (of) to indicate possession or association, meaning "of the doctor."

Extra sentences:  
• "Hij is met zijn vriend, in de bibliotheek." (He is with his friend, in the library.)  
• "Zij zit in de tuin van haar oma." (She is sitting in the garden of her grandmother.)  
• "We praten met de leraar, in het klaslokaal." (We talk with the teacher, in the classroom.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Pieter is met Anna, in het café aan de hoek." (Pieter is with Anna, in the café on the corner.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it is common for doctors to have a "spreekkamer" or consultation room where they meet with patients for discussions and examinations. This is distinct from the treatment or examination room, highlighting the emphasis on patient-doctor communication.

sentences.nl: Dan kan ze helpen,, want zijn Nederlands is nog niet zo goed.
sentences.en: Then she can help, because his Dutch is not that good yet.

sentences.nl: Ondertussen wacht Martin in de wachtkamer.
sentences.en: Meanwhile, Martin is waiting in the waiting room.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Meanwhile waits Martin in the waiting room.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ondertussen" is an adverb meaning "meanwhile," indicating simultaneous actions.  
• The sentence uses the present tense. In Dutch, the verb "wacht" (waits) precedes the subject "Martin" in main clauses.  
• "In de wachtkamer" is a prepositional phrase indicating location.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ondertussen kookt zij het avondeten." (Meanwhile, she is cooking dinner.)  
  - "Hij leest een boek in de bibliotheek." (He is reading a book in the library.)  
  - "Ondertussen regent het buiten." (Meanwhile, it is raining outside.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ondertussen maakt zij haar huiswerk." (Meanwhile, she is doing her homework.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Waiting rooms ("wachtkamers") are common in doctor's offices and hospitals in the Netherlands, often equipped with magazines and sometimes even coffee machines to make the wait more comfortable.

sentences.nl: Hij is een beetje verdrietig.
sentences.en: He is a little sad.

sentences.nl: Hij wilde met Marieke naar het meertje,, om samen romantisch naar de maan te kijken.
sentences.en: He wanted to go to the lake with Marieke to romantically watch the moon together.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He wanted with Marieke to the little lake, to together romantically at the moon to look.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij wilde" uses the past tense of the modal verb "willen" (to want).  
• "Met Marieke naar het meertje" shows the use of "met" (with) to indicate accompaniment and "naar" (to) for direction.  
• The phrase "om samen romantisch naar de maan te kijken" uses "om... te" to indicate purpose or intention, often followed by an infinitive verb.  
• Example: "Ze kwam om te helpen." (She came to help.)  
• Example: "Ik lees een boek om te ontspannen." (I read a book to relax.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij ging met zijn broer naar het park, om samen te voetballen. (He went with his brother to the park, to play soccer together.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Romantic walks or outings by small lakes or ponds are common in Dutch leisure culture, especially in the countryside or nature reserves.

sentences.nl: Maar nu zijn ze bij de dokter.
sentences.en: But now they are at the doctor's.

sentences.nl: De huisarts vraagt: ‘waar heb je pijn?’, eh… hier… mijn been doet zeer… en mijn knie.
sentences.en: The doctor asks: 'where does it hurt?', uh... here... my leg hurts... and my knee.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The general practitioner asks: 'where have you pain?', uh… here… my leg does sore… and my knee.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De huisarts" means "the general practitioner" or "family doctor."  
• "waar heb je pijn?" translates to "where do you have pain?" The Dutch use "hebben" (to have) with "pijn" (pain) to express feeling pain, similar to "having pain" in English.  
• "doet zeer" means "does sore" or "hurts." This is a common way to express pain in Dutch.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Waar heb je last van?" (What are you suffering from?)  
  - "Mijn hoofd doet pijn." (My head hurts.)  
  - "Hij heeft pijn in zijn rug." (He has pain in his back.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De tandarts vraagt: 'hebt u ergens pijn?' (The dentist asks: 'do you have any pain anywhere?')

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, a "huisarts" is often the first point of contact for health issues and plays a crucial role in the healthcare system, similar to a family doctor in other countries.

sentences.nl: Kleed je maar even uit…
sentences.en: Just take your clothes off...
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Get dressed yourself but for a moment out...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Kleed je uit" is a reflexive verb phrase meaning "undress yourself." "Je" is a reflexive pronoun.  
• "Maar" here is used to soften the command, making it more casual or polite, similar to "just" or "go ahead" in English.  
• "Even" adds the sense of "just for a moment" or "briefly," often used to indicate a short duration or a quick action.

Extra examples:  
• "Doe je jas maar uit." (Take off your jacket.)  
• "Ga maar zitten." (Go ahead and sit down.)  
• "Wacht even hier." (Wait here for a moment.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Doe je schoenen maar even uit." (Just take off your shoes for a moment.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it's common to be direct with instructions or requests, but using words like "maar" and "even" can soften the tone and make it sound more polite or informal.

sentences.nl: Eh…
sentences.en: Uh...

sentences.nl: Je mag je ondergoed aanhouden hoor.
sentences.en: You can keep your underwear on, you know.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You may your underwear keep on, hear.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je mag" means "you may" or "you are allowed to," indicating permission.  
• "Aanhouden" is a separable verb meaning "to keep on" or "to leave on." In Dutch, separable verbs often split, with the prefix moving to the end of the clause.  
• "Hoor" is an informal particle used to emphasize or soften a statement, similar to "you know" or "okay."

Examples:  
– "Je mag hier niet roken." (You are not allowed to smoke here.)  
– "Zij houdt haar schoenen aan." (She keeps her shoes on.)  
– "Dat is niet erg, hoor." (That's not a problem, you know.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Je mag het boek meenemen hoor." (You may take the book with you, okay.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Hoor" is often used in informal settings and can convey friendliness or reassurance. It's a way to make a statement sound less harsh or more conversational.

sentences.nl: OK.
sentences.en: OK.

sentences.nl: Ik begrijp het Gianluca.
sentences.en: I understand, Gianluca.

sentences.nl: Marieke kijkt naar de andere kant.
sentences.en: Marieke looks to the other side.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke looks at the other side.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Kijkt naar" is a verb-preposition combination where "kijken" (to look) requires the preposition "naar" (at).  
• "De andere kant" means "the other side," where "de" is the definite article, "andere" means "other," and "kant" means "side."  
• Word order follows the Subject-Verb-Object rule typical in simple Dutch sentences.

• Extra Phrases:  
  - "Hij kijkt naar de vogels." (He looks at the birds.)  
  - "Zij kijkt naar haar horloge." (She looks at her watch.)  
  - "Wij kijken naar de film." (We watch the movie.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Pieter kijkt naar zijn schoenen. (Pieter looks at his shoes.)

sentences.nl: De dokter onderzoekt Gianluca…
sentences.en: The doctor examines Gianluca…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The doctor examines Gianluca...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De dokter" is the subject, meaning "The doctor." "Onderzoekt" is the present tense of "onderzoeken," meaning "to examine." It follows the subject-verb-object order typical in Dutch main clauses.  
• The sentence uses the present tense, which is often used in Dutch to describe current actions or habitual activities.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "De leraar leest een boek." (The teacher reads a book.)  
  - "De kat vangt een muis." (The cat catches a mouse.)  
  - "De chef kookt het avondeten." (The chef cooks the dinner.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De verpleegster helpt de patiënt. (The nurse helps the patient.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, visiting a doctor (huisarts) is often the first step in healthcare, and they will refer you to specialists if needed. The use of a professional title like "dokter" is common and indicates respect for their expertise.

sentences.nl: Twintig jaar geleden woonde ik in ItaliÎ.
sentences.en: Twenty years ago, I lived in Italy.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Twenty years ago lived I in Italy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the past tense "woonde," which is the simple past (imperfect) of "wonen" (to live).  
• "Twintig jaar geleden" (Twenty years ago) shows time and is placed at the beginning for emphasis.  
• The structure "woonde ik" (lived I) follows the subject-verb inversion common in sentences that start with a time expression.

• Examples:  
  - "Tien jaar geleden werkte hij als leraar." (Ten years ago he worked as a teacher.)  
  - "Vorig jaar reisden we naar Frankrijk." (Last year we traveled to France.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Vijf jaar geleden ontmoette ik mijn beste vriend." (Five years ago I met my best friend.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Italy is often a popular destination for Dutch people, both for vacations and for longer stays, due to its warm climate, rich history, and cuisine.

sentences.nl: Ik werkte daar als assistent.
sentences.en: I worked there as an assistant.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I worked there as assistant.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik werkte" is the past tense of "werken" (to work). The -te ending indicates simple past tense for weak verbs.  
• "Daar" means "there," indicating location.  
• "Als" is used to indicate the role or function someone has, similar to "as" in English.

• Examples:  
  - "Wij speelden daar als kinderen." (We played there as children.)  
  - "Hij werkte hier als leraar." (He worked here as a teacher.)  
  - "Zij zong daar als solist." (She sang there as a soloist.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij werkte daar als manager." (She worked there as a manager.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No culture note.

sentences.nl: En toen leerde ik Italiaans.
sentences.en: And then I learned Italian.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then learned I Italian.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En toen" means "and then" and is used to indicate a sequence of events.  
• "Leerde" is the past tense of "leren" (to learn). In Dutch, the simple past is used to describe completed actions in the past.  
• "Ik" is the subject pronoun "I".  
• Word order in main clauses is typically Subject-Verb-Object, but in sentences starting with a time element like "en toen," the verb follows immediately after.  
• "Italiaans" is the Dutch word for "Italian," referring to the language.

• Example Sentences:  
  – "En toen ging ik naar huis." (And then I went home.)  
  – "En toen zag ik hem niet meer." (And then I didn't see him anymore.)  
  – "Ik leerde Duits op school." (I learned German at school.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En toen begon het te regenen." (And then it started to rain.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Learning languages is often emphasized in Dutch education, with English, French, and German commonly taught in schools. Italian might be learned for personal interest or specific professional reasons.

sentences.nl: Mijn docent was heel erg knap.
sentences.en: My teacher was very handsome.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• My teacher was very very handsome.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Mijn docent" (My teacher) is a possessive phrase where "mijn" is a possessive pronoun.  
• "Was" is the past tense of "zijn" (to be).  
• "Heel erg" is an intensifier meaning "very very," and is often used for emphasis. "Knap" means "handsome" or "good-looking."

• Extra phrases:  
  - Zij was heel erg blij. (She was very very happy.)  
  - Het was heel erg koud buiten. (It was very very cold outside.)  
  - Ik ben heel erg moe. (I am very very tired.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Mijn hond is heel erg speels. (My dog is very very playful.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Knap" can describe attractiveness in both appearance and intelligence. In the Netherlands, academic or intellectual achievements are often appreciated, so "knap" can imply both good looks and being smart.

sentences.nl: Daarom wilde ik alleen maar studeren.
sentences.en: That's why I just wanted to study.

sentences.en: I wanted to be her best student.

sentences.nl: Ik kende het hele woordenboek uit mijn hoofd.
sentences.en: I knew the entire dictionary by heart.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I knew the whole dictionary from my head.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik kende" is the past tense of "kennen" (to know), indicating a past state of knowledge.  
• "Het hele woordenboek" means "the whole dictionary," where "hele" (whole) modifies "woordenboek" (dictionary).  
• "Uit mijn hoofd" literally translates to "from my head," an expression meaning "by heart" or "memorized."

• Example phrases:  
  - "Ik kende de tekst uit mijn hoofd." (I knew the text by heart.)  
  - "Zij leerde de liedjes uit haar hoofd." (She learned the songs by heart.)  
  - "Hij kende het verhaal uit zijn hoofd." (He knew the story by heart.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hij kende alle hoofdsteden uit zijn hoofd." (He knew all the capitals by heart.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Knowing something "uit je hoofd" often indicates a deep level of familiarity or mastery, which can be valued in educational and professional settings in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: En toen? — Toen trouwde ze met mij!
sentences.en: And then? — Then she married me!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then? — Then married she with me!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Toen" is used here as a conjunction meaning "then" to indicate a sequence of events.  
• "Trouwde" is the simple past tense of "trouwen" (to marry). The simple past is often used in storytelling.  
• "Met" is a preposition meaning "with," commonly used with "trouwen" to indicate whom someone married.

Examples:  
• "Toen ging hij naar huis." (Then he went home.)  
• "Ze trouwde met een arts." (She married a doctor.)  
• "Toen kwam de regen." (Then the rain came.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En toen? — Toen kocht hij een huis!" (And then? — Then he bought a house!)  

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: Hoorde je dat Marieke? — Hij trouwde met zijn docent!
sentences.en: Did you hear that, Marieke? — He married his teacher!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Heard you that Marieke? — He married with his teacher!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoorde je dat" is a past tense question structure, where "hoorde" is the simple past of "horen" (to hear). In questions, the verb comes first.  
• "Trouwen met" means "to marry with," and "met" is the preposition used with "trouwen." Unlike in English, where one says "marry someone," Dutch uses "met" (with).  
• "Zijn docent" means "his teacher," where "zijn" is the possessive pronoun for "his."

Examples:  
• "Zag je dat, Pieter?" (Did you see that, Pieter?)  
• "Hij danste met zijn vriendin." (He danced with his girlfriend.)  
• "Ze leerde van haar fouten." (She learned from her mistakes.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Vergeet je dat niet, Anna? — Hij werkte met zijn broer." (Don't you forget that, Anna? — He worked with his brother.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, addressing someone directly by name in a conversation, as in "Marieke," is common and reflects a direct communication style.

sentences.nl: Volgens mij is dit een gevalletje ‘aanstelleritis’.
sentences.en: I think this is a case of 'hypochondria'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• According to me is this a little case of ‘pretending to be sick’.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Volgens mij" translates to "according to me" and is often used to express personal opinions or beliefs.  
• The word "gevalletje" is a diminutive form of "geval" (case), which can imply a lighthearted or somewhat dismissive tone.  
• "Aanstelleritis" is a colloquial term combining "aansteller" (someone who exaggerates or pretends) and "-itis" (a suffix usually used for diseases), humorously suggesting that someone is pretending to be ill.

Extra phrases:  
• "Volgens hem is het een slecht idee." (According to him, it is a bad idea.)  
• "Dit is een gevalletje overmacht." (This is a case of force majeure.)  
• "Ze heeft altijd last van aanstelleritis." (She always suffers from 'pretending to be sick'.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Volgens haar is dit gewoon pech. (According to her, this is just bad luck.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The term "aanstelleritis" is often used humorously in the Netherlands to describe someone who is exaggerating their symptoms or situation, similar to calling someone a hypochondriac in a light-hearted way.

sentences.nl: ‘Aanstelleritis’, daar heb ik nog nooit van gehoord.
sentences.en: 'Aanstelleritis', I've never heard of that.

sentences.nl: Ik ben zelf ook arts, cardioloog…. maar dat woord ken ik niet.
sentences.en: I am also a doctor myself, a cardiologist... but I don't know that word.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I am myself also doctor, cardiologist... but that word know I not.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ben" (I am) is the present tense of "zijn" (to be).  
• "Zelf" reinforces the subject, meaning "myself" in this context.  
• "Ook" means "also," showing addition.  
• "Ken ik niet" uses inversion, common in Dutch when the object precedes the verb; it translates to "I don't know".

• Example 1: "Ik ben zelf ook leraar." (I am myself also a teacher.)  
• Example 2: "Dat begrijp ik niet." (I don't understand that.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik ben zelf ook muzikant, maar dat instrument ken ik niet." (I am also a musician, but I don't know that instrument.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it's not uncommon for people to be direct about what they don't know, as seen in "maar dat woord ken ik niet." This directness often comes across as honesty and clarity in communication.

sentences.nl: Gianluca kijkt naar Marieke…

sentences.nl: Sorry Gianluca, ik ken geen vertaling.
sentences.en: Sorry Gianluca, I don't know a translation.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Sorry Gianluca, I know no translation.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Sorry" is a direct borrowing from English and is commonly used in Dutch to express regret.  
• "Ik ken geen vertaling" means "I know no translation." "Ken" is the first-person singular of "kennen," meaning "to know" in the sense of familiarity. "Geen" is used to negate nouns.  
• "Ik ken geen" is a common structure for expressing unfamiliarity:  
  - "Ik ken geen antwoord." (I know no answer.)  
  - "Ik ken geen oplossing." (I know no solution.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Sorry, ik ken geen liedje dat zo begint. (Sorry, I know no song that starts like that.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Names such as "Gianluca" suggest a conversation with someone of Italian heritage, which reflects the multicultural nature of Dutch society. The Netherlands is home to many people from diverse backgrounds, and it is common to encounter non-Dutch names.

sentences.nl: Dokter, wat is het medicijn? — In Nederland hebben we maar één medicijn, tegen ‘aanstelleritis’.
sentences.en: Doctor, what is the medicine? — In the Netherlands, we have only one medicine, against 'attention-seeking syndrome'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Doctor, what is the medicine? — In the Netherlands we have only one medicine, against 'pretending-to-be-sick-itis'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "maar één" to mean "only one," which is a common way to express limitation.  
• "tegen" translates to "against" and is often used with ailments or conditions.  
• Example: "Er is maar één weg naar huis." (There is only one road home.)  
• Example: "Hij is allergisch tegen stof." (He is allergic to dust.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Er is maar één oplossing tegen verveling. (There is only one solution for boredom.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The term 'aanstelleritis' humorously refers to someone exaggerating their illness. It reflects a cultural attitude in the Netherlands that values being straightforward and not overly dramatic about minor inconveniences.

sentences.nl: En dat is? — Kusje d’r op!
sentences.en: And what is that? — Kiss it better!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And that is? — Little kiss on it!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence "En dat is?" is a question that implies a follow-up or clarification is needed. "Kusje" is a diminutive form of "kus" (kiss), indicating something small or affectionate. "D’r" is a contraction of "daar" (there) and "op" (on), which is a colloquial way to say "there on it."  
• Example: "Ik heb een plekje, kusje d’r op?" (I have a spot, kiss on it?)  
• Example: "Doe er een pleister op." (Put a band-aid on it.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Heb je pijn? Kusje d’r op!" (Are you in pain? Little kiss on it!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "Kusje d’r op" is a common, affectionate way to comfort someone, especially children, when they have a minor injury like a scrape or bruise. It reflects a nurturing attitude and the belief in the comforting power of a simple gesture.

sentences.nl: En? — Gianluca zegt: ‘het is niet ernstig’
sentences.en: And? — Gianluca says: 'it is not serious'
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And? — Gianluca says: 'it is not serious'

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with "En?" which is a common way to prompt someone to continue or explain further, similar to saying "And?" in English.  
• "Het is niet ernstig" is a simple declarative sentence in Dutch, consisting of a subject "het" (it), a verb "is" (is), and a negation "niet" (not) followed by the adjective "ernstig" (serious). Dutch typically follows Subject-Verb-Object order.  
• Example 1: "Het is niet belangrijk." (It is not important.)  
• Example 2: "Het is niet koud." (It is not cold.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En? — Maria antwoordt: ‘het is niet nodig’ (And? — Maria replies: 'it is not necessary')

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: Ik krijg een medicijn en dan ben ik genezen.
sentences.en: I receive a medicine and then I am cured.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I get a medicine and then am I cured.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik krijg" uses the present tense of "krijgen" (to get/receive), indicating a future action in this context.  
• "En dan" means "and then," showing a sequence of actions.  
• "Ben ik genezen" uses "ben" (am) and "genezen" (cured), with "genezen" functioning as a past participle used adjectivally here.  
• Extra phrases:  
  - "Ik krijg een boek en dan lees ik het." (I get a book and then I read it.)  
  - "Ze krijgt een cadeau en dan opent ze het." (She receives a gift and then she opens it.)  
  - "We eten en dan gaan we naar huis." (We eat and then we go home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik krijg een uitnodiging en dan ga ik naar het feest." (I receive an invitation and then I go to the party.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the healthcare system is well-regarded, and receiving medication from a doctor or pharmacy is a common and trusted process.

sentences.nl: Kom nog een keertje Martin.
sentences.en: Come again sometime, Martin.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Come another time Martin.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Kom" is the imperative form of "komen," which means "to come." In Dutch, the imperative is often just the stem of the verb.  
• "Nog een keertje" is an informal way of saying "again" or "another time." "Nog" means "still" or "again," "een" means "a," and "keertje" is the diminutive form of "keer," meaning "time" or "instance." The diminutive adds a sense of casualness or endearment.  
• "Martin" is the person being addressed, placed at the end of the sentence for emphasis.

Extra Examples:  
• "Kom maar binnen." (Come on in.)  
• "Probeer het nog een keertje." (Try it once more.)  
• "Zeg het nog eens." (Say it again.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Bel nog een keertje als je tijd hebt." (Call again if you have time.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Kom nog een keertje" is a casual, friendly way to invite someone to visit again, often used among friends or family. It reflects the Dutch informal and direct communication style.

sentences.nl: We regelen wel een slaapplek voor jou.
sentences.en: We'll arrange a place to sleep for you.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We arrange surely a sleeping place for you.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "We regelen wel" uses "wel" to convey reassurance, similar to "surely" or "don't worry."  
• "Een slaapplek" is a compound noun made of "slaap" (sleep) and "plek" (place), meaning a place to sleep.  
• Word order: The sentence follows the standard Dutch structure: Subject (We) – Verb (regelen) – Adverb (wel) – Object (een slaapplek) – Prepositional phrase (voor jou).  

Extra phrases:  
• "Ik koop wel een cadeau voor haar." (I will surely buy a gift for her.)  
• "We vinden wel een oplossing." (We will surely find a solution.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ze regelen wel wat te eten voor ons." (They will surely arrange some food for us.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of "wel" in Dutch can often convey a sense of reassurance and confidence, a common conversational tool in Dutch to put someone at ease.

sentences.nl: Tot zover de les van vandaag.
sentences.en: So much for today's lesson.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Until so far the lesson of today.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Tot zover" is a phrase used to indicate completion or conclusion up to this point.  
• "De les van vandaag" means "the lesson of today," with "de" as the definite article and "van" indicating possession or relation.  

Extra phrases:  
– "Tot zover alles duidelijk?" (Is everything clear so far?)  
– "Tot zover de presentatie." (That's the presentation so far.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Tot zover mijn uitleg." (That's my explanation so far.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• This phrase is often used by teachers or presenters in the Netherlands to informally wrap up a session or segment, indicating that the main content has been covered.

sentences.nl: Het blijft spannend.

sentences.nl: Voor wie kiest Marieke? — Tot de volgende keer bij ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: Who does Marieke choose? — Until next time on ‘Are you in the mood?’
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• For whom chooses Marieke? — Until the next time at 'Are you excited?'

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Voor wie" is a question phrase meaning "for whom," indicating the object of the choice.  
• "Kiest" is the present tense of "kiezen" (to choose), and it follows the subject "Marieke," demonstrating subject-verb inversion in questions.  
• "Tot de volgende keer" is a common phrase meaning "until next time," often used to end a conversation or show.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Voor wie is dit cadeau?" (For whom is this gift?)  
  - "Tot de volgende week!" (Until next week!)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Voor wie werkt hij?" (For whom does he work?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Heb je zin?" can refer to a Dutch television or radio show, playing on the Dutch phrase "Heb je zin?" which means "Are you excited?" or "Do you feel like it?"
